clue.text: Some Christians stoned going to Charlotte?

parts.note: stoned on drugs is high
Charlotte Church is a Welsh singer, so her surname is wanted

explanation.surface: A group of churchgoers on drugs heading off to a city called Charlotte.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlotte looks like the North Carolina city; the question mark warns it is a person, the singer Charlotte Church.
explanation.definitionFit: High Church Anglicans favour ritual and ceremony, so they are one group among Christian believers.

clue.text: Game where every player gets stick

definitions.text: Game where every player gets stick

parts.words: Game where every player gets stick
parts.note: surface reading: a sport in which every player is criticised; setter's reading: every player is handed a stick to play with

explanation.walkthrough: To get stick is British slang for being criticised, which makes this sound like a cruel team; literally each player is issued a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Every player in this team sport carries a curved stick to strike the ball or puck.

clue.text: Gnu put up with hog running outside, excited

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up turns it bottom to top
being outside means wrapping round something else
running freely suggests letters on the loose and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An antelope tolerates a pig charging around it in great excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: GNU is turned upward to UNG, and the letters of HOG are rearranged as G...HO and placed either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gung-ho describes someone overly eager and enthusiastic, which matches being worked up or keen.

clue.text: Perceptive about Bard's King Edward hiding sad expression

indicators.note: what hides something keeps it tucked inside

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
King Lear is a Shakespeare play, the Bard being Shakespeare
Ted is a short form of Edward
a sigh expresses sadness

explanation.surface: A comment on how shrewd a tearful Shakespearean king is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' reads as one monarch, but King belongs with the Bard, and Edward is split off as his short name; the sad expression sits between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clear-sighted sees situations accurately and with insight, just as a perceptive person does.

clue.text: Regularly avoiding nyala, gnu's going over plain

indicators.note: going over, in a down clue, tips the letters back on themselves
skipping letters at a steady interval leaves every other one

parts.note: the even letters of these two animal names

explanation.surface: One antelope steers clear of another while crossing open grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: A nyala is an African antelope. 'Plain' looks like grassland for the animals, but it is the definition, meaning unattractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain, of a person's looks, is a polite way to say unattractive, which is the blunt sense of the answer.

clue.text: May in Paris: from the feminine attire, things brightening up

parts.note: may and can both express permission
French for 'of the' before a feminine noun is de la
a bra is an item of attire

explanation.surface: Springtime in Paris, with women's fashions cheering everything up.
explanation.walkthrough: May looks like the month in Paris, but it is the verb, and 'in Paris' marks only the French words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Candelabra are branched holders for several candles, which light up a room or table.

clue.text: Fashionable greetings cards originally posted by Charlie

indicators.note: placed next to, so one piece is set alongside another

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
hi is a greeting

indicators.note: what comes originally is at the start, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Stylish greetings cards sent off by someone called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posted' suggests the mail; here it means placed beside, so Charlie's C comes before HI and the first letter of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant, the quality of being in fashion.

clue.text: Personnel smuggling gold — if caught around Italy, that's scary

indicators.note: smuggled goods are carried hidden inside something
going around something means enclosing it

parts.note: HR, human resources, is the personnel department
or is gold in heraldry
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Staff smuggling gold face a frightening fate if arrested in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold as 'or' is heraldic, and caught as 'c' comes from cricket scorecards; both conventions are worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something horrific causes horror, so it is frightening or appalling; 'that's' turns the definition into a description.

clue.text: Come Together using fiddle? Extreme!

parts.note: a fiddle is a swindle, a con
the verge is the extreme edge of something

explanation.surface: Playing the Beatles' Come Together on a violin is an extreme idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make 'Come Together' look like the Beatles song title, and fiddle looks like a violin; it is a con.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or people that converge move towards each other and meet at one point.

clue.text: Alice detailed 20 changes for tube fare

indicators.note: changes means alters the order, so these letters are rearranged
detailed means with its tail cut off, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the name Alice, without its final letter
the answer to 20 down, the singer John Lennon

explanation.surface: Alice and a numbered character swapping places, or changing trains on the Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts ALICE to ALIC, and '20' brings in the answer to 20 down; 'changes' rearranges both together. Tube fare is food shaped like tubes, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannelloni are large tubes of pasta, stuffed and baked, so they are a tube-shaped dish.

clue.text: Rejected or covered by popular press

indicators.note: a covering goes round what it covers

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so it runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something either turned down or reported in the tabloid newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular press' looks like the tabloids, but press is the definition, and popular only supplies the covering letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them flat with a heated appliance.

clue.text: Decorate with sugar paste before cake topped — it looks tasty!

parts.note: to ice a cake is to decorate it with a sugar coating
to paste someone is to beat them soundly, as is to cream them

indicators.note: topped means with its top cut off, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a scone is a small plain cake

explanation.surface: Baking instructions: ice it, add a paste, then finish the cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paste' is not a baking paste but slang for thrashing, as is cream. 'topped' takes the first letter off SCONE, a small British teatime cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone filled with ice cream is a tempting treat, the sort of thing that looks delicious.

clue.text: Urge former partner to go with trunks, not smalls

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: S is the abbreviation for small, and not smalls removes the Ss, which here are the word's first and last letters

parts.note: swimming trunks are shorts

explanation.surface: An ex insisting on swimming trunks rather than underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Smalls is British slang for underwear, but here it means more than one S, for small: 'not smalls' takes both Ss off SHORTS, leaving HORT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort someone is to urge or strongly encourage them to act.

clue.text: Draw has clubs involved in spicy derbies

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be drawn inside it
spicy suggests something hot and lively, so letters get stirred

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A drawn match between clubs in heated local derbies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' reads as a tied football match, which suits clubs and derbies; it means to trace a shape, as in describing a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry you describe a circle or arc by tracing its outline, which is drawing it.

clue.text: Decide a list I compiled is somewhat impractical

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of something, so a stretch of the text is taken

parts.note: the run of letters starting inside the first word

explanation.surface: A judgement that a list someone drew up is rather unrealistic.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from inside 'Decide' to the first letter of 'compiled'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealistic plan pursues perfect principles over practical realities, so it can be unrealistic and unworkable.

clue.text: Spotting what flies try, circling river bank, to conceal hatch, heading off

indicators.note: circling means going round, so these letters surround the other one

parts.note: to bid is to try, as in a bid for power

indicators.note: to conceal means to hide inside, so these letters go round the other piece

parts.note: to bank and to wing can both mean to tilt in flight, as an aircraft turning

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: the word hatch, without its first letter

explanation.surface: A fly fisher trying a river bank to hide what is hatching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try circling river' gives BID around R; 'bank to conceal hatch, heading off' puts ATCH, which is HATCH minus its first letter, inside WING.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdwatching is observing birds in the wild, and birds are creatures that fly.

clue.text: Roughly scour gnu's midsection and head with bottom of coarse sponge

indicators.note: done roughly, the letters are handled without care and jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the midsection of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the centre of the three-letter animal

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the same animal

indicators.note: the bottom of a down word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Cleaning a wildebeest's belly and head with a rough sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' looks like the cleaning tool in the surface; it is the verb, to live off others.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge off people is to cadge things from them without paying, the same as to scrounge.

clue.text: Perhaps 1 across Central Chicago has herb topping?

indicators.note: topping means sitting above, so in this down answer this piece goes first

parts.note: basil is a herb
the middle letters of Chicago

explanation.surface: A Chicago dish with herbs sprinkled on top.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'topping' puts BASIL above ICA, the central letters of CHICAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a grand church, of the kind used for elaborate, ritual-rich Christian worship.

clue.text: Indiscreet book put in shopping bag — it's a safeguard by the way

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside another thing

parts.note: a carrier bag is a British plastic shopping bag
rash means reckless or unwise
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A gossipy book slipped into a shopping bag is described, by the way, as a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' reads as an aside; it means beside the road, which is where a crash barrier stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash barrier is a fence along a road or motorway that protects vehicles which leave the carriageway.

clue.text: Plummeting income initially needs to be 10 times as much

indicators.text: initially needs to be 10 times as much
indicators.note: the first letter, read as a Roman numeral, must be swapped for the numeral worth ten times it

parts.note: your living is the income you earn

explanation.surface: A grim note that falling income must somehow be multiplied by ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially needs to be 10 times as much' reads the first letter of LIVING as a Roman numeral: L is 50, and ten times that is 500, D.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving bird or aircraft is plunging steeply downwards, which is plummeting.

clue.text: Christmas with breaking news about singer

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way
breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
N is new, doubled for the plural, as pp is pages

explanation.surface: Breaking news at Christmas about a famous singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking news' reads as a headline, but breaking signals insertion and news gives two Ns. John Lennon of the Beatles also sang Happy Xmas (War Is Over).
explanation.definitionFit: John Lennon was the Beatles singer and songwriter, so the definition names him by his job.

clue.text: Breathe in oxygen repeatedly — one litre, healthy stuff!

indicators.note: in places the breathing word between the two oxygen symbols

parts.note: O is oxygen's chemical symbol, given twice
to breathe is to be alive, to live
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Take a deep breath of air, then a litre of something good for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive oil is a cooking fat often praised as part of a wholesome Mediterranean diet.

clue.text: Conservative MP I reported is circumventing rule

indicators.note: to circumvent is to surround, so the answer lies inside the words around it

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the last

explanation.surface: A Tory MP who was reported for getting round the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circumventing rule' reads as evading a regulation; rule is the definition, and the text before is wrapped around the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Empire can mean supreme power or sovereignty over territory, the sense of rule as dominion.

clue.text: Wildebeest with no tail, aged one taking little bites

indicators.note: with no tail means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a gnu is a wildebeest
Chambers gives at as 'having reached the age of', as in at 60

explanation.surface: An old, tailless wildebeest nibbling at its food.
explanation.walkthrough: Aged 60 and at 60 mean the same, so aged gives AT; 'with no tail' cuts GNU to GN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small biting fly, so it is a creature that gives tiny bites.

clue.text: Trouble following knight's arrest

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so this goes second

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Problems in the wake of a knight being taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive but is 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a criminal is informal for catching and arresting them.

clue.text: Rubbish catches all round — Botham maybe getting thunderous

indicators.note: turning all the way round sets things facing backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
nets catch fish
Ian Botham is a famous English cricketer

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: Botham, the great all-rounder, takes catches as fans roar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catches all round' plays on cricket's all-rounder; really the rubbish and the catches are turned round together as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentorian describes an extremely loud, booming voice, after Stentor, a loud-voiced herald in Homer.

clue.text: Articles Spanish and English put together in style

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article
an is an English indefinite article

explanation.surface: Spanish and English pieces of writing combined with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' looks like pieces of writing; it means grammatical articles, one from each language.
explanation.definitionFit: Élan is energetic flair and confidence, a stylish dash in how something is done.

clue.text: Random way to encounter gnu?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: haphazard, unfocused, as an adjective
second meaning, cryptic: scatter the letters of the animal and you meet a firearm

explanation.surface: Wondering whether bumping into a wildebeest is just down to chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags wordplay: scatter the letters of GNU and you get GUN, and a shotgun is also a way to meet a gnu on safari.
explanation.definitionFit: A scattergun approach is indiscriminate and unfocused, like shot spraying widely from a shotgun.
